A1.justification: Both PDFs describe V2XPnP and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Text comparison and visual inspection support a reliable comparison of the complete versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original cooperative perception and prediction experiments, component ablations, communication robustness tests, and additional task benchmarks in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–3 and S1–S3 and the robustness experiments in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The PointPillar backbone, temporal and spatial attention modules, map fusion, prediction heads, losses, and staged training procedure remain unchanged. Figure 3's revised labels and organization do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same V2XPnP-Sequential dataset, collaboration modes, and end-to-end, temporal perception, and traditional prediction tasks. The revised scenario counts do not establish a change in represented domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1 and S1–S3 and Figure 6. This includes the adapted fusion baselines, early/late/no-fusion configurations, and the Attention and LSTM predictors.

E3.justification: Section 4 revises the dataset from 100 to 96 scenarios, including 42 to 38 V2V scenarios; Section 4.1 changes newly annotated scenarios from 32 to 28. Section 5.1 changes the training/validation/test split from 80/6/14 to 76/6/14. Other settings remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The communication-strategy comparison, component ablations, compression and communication-noise tests, and qualitative examples are retained. Appendices C and D preserve the analyses of joint-task optimization and prediction under imperfect perception.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 6 retains the same injected-noise settings, which are robustness conditions rather than statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and S1–S4 retain the same entries and numerical values, and Figures 5–6 retain identical result images. For example, V2XPnP's vehicle-centric AP and EPA remain 71.6% and 48.2%. The revised training split does not establish a performance gain.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and S1–S3, mathematical task formulations, and associated reasoning are unchanged. The bounding-box description is rephrased without changing its mathematical content.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a unified V2X perception-and-prediction framework, a real-world sequential dataset supporting all collaboration modes, and benchmarks of 11 fusion models with superior proposed-method performance. Revised dataset accounting does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning temporal information, occlusion mitigation, map guidance, and communication efficiency remain unchanged. The appendices retain the same qualifications about joint-task optimization and prediction's dependence on perception quality.

D1.justification: v2's abstract promises future release of the codebase and dataset; v3 omits that statement while retaining the project link. This changes the release disclosure without establishing actual release or withdrawal. Appendix implementation and data-processing details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 57 references and substantive comparisons with earlier research are retained. Reference reflow and a changed citation page locator do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and grammar edits, revises the introductory dataset breakdown, updates correspondence information, and adds acknowledgements. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4 are redrawn or restyled, particularly Figure 3's explicit backbone labels and regrouped attention blocks. Figure 1 drops its framework headings. Tables and result figures are retained, with limited spacing and placement changes that bring the complete conclusion onto page 8.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves exposition through Figure 3's clearer backbone labels and attention-module grouping, along with a more explicit introductory dataset breakdown. Scientific evidence remains unchanged. The unexplained training-split revision and less explicit release information limit reproducibility clarity, so the overall gain is confined mainly to presentation.
